**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Take a published claim apart. Name the specific failure. Say which direction it pushes the estimate, and whether more data would fix it.

## Where to read more

[Remix](https://mixtape.scunning.com/) ch. 5 on unconfoundedness, for what conditioning can and cannot fix. [Adams](https://doi.org/10.4135/9788132108498) ch. 14 on reliability and validity.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Bias first. Omitted variables, sorting and selection, measurement error — classical and not — and reverse causality. For each: what it does to the estimate, and in which direction. Then false precision, which is the quieter problem. Dependence ignored. Multiple testing. Specification search. The number stays where it is and the error bar shrinks around it.

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

First, together: one published claim, taken apart. Which failure is doing the damage? Would more data fix it? Then the same move on a paper from your own literature. Write down the one threat your design will have to survive. You will be answering it in November.

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
